newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania Litimpeks talks with Estonians, Poles.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania Litimpeks talks with Estonians, Poles.

text.p: Lithuania's Litimpeks, once a top bank but at the centre of a bank crisis in late 1995, said on Friday it was talking on selling a stake to Estonian Tallinna Pank and Polish Kredyt Bank.

"We have been working with Polish and Estonian banks all week," Gintautas Preidys, the chairman of the bank's board, told a news conference, confirming that the banks were Tallinna Pank and Kredyt Bank.
Litimpeks, reopened last June after being shut by the central bank in December 1995, has faced an uphill struggle to stay in business.
It has pinned its hopes on a 60 million litas share issue which it will submit to the securities commission on Friday.
"It seems we will have one strategic investor who might buy a 30 to 50 percent stake in our new issue," Preidys said.
"I don't think that all of the buyers will be foreign investors," he said.
He added that the bank would like to see the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) among its partners.
"We would like to finish our talks by May 20," he said.
Tallinna Pank earlier said it was eyeing opportunities in Lithuania and was negotiating with several Lithuanian banks.
Several leading Estonian banks have said that they want to open in Lithuania, the largest of the Baltic states and the one which was hit most recently by a bank crisis.
Kredyt Bank last year became the first foreign bank to receive permission to set up a branch office in Lithuania.
